title: The First Letter to the Corinthians Timeline
sub: Divisions, the Cross, and the Resurrection of the Dead
desc: A church fractured by factions, lawsuits, and immorality is answered chapter by chapter: the foolishness of the cross, spiritual gifts ranked by love, and the New Testament's fullest defense of the bodily resurrection.

eras.label: Era One · 1 Corinthians 1
eras.name: Divisions in Corinth — Christ Crucified, the Wisdom of God
eras.dates: A fractious, status-obsessed church divided into personality cults, answered with the deliberate foolishness of a crucified Messiah

events.title: Greeting and Thanksgiving: Not Lacking in Any Gift
events.detail: Paul thanks God for a church rich in speech and knowledge despite everything about to go wrong in the rest of the letter, setting up the tension between their spiritual gifting and their spiritual immaturity.

verses.text: “God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.”

events.title: Quarrels: ‘I Am of Paul,’ ‘I of Apollos,’ ‘I of Cephas’
events.detail: Paul names the problem behind the whole letter: the church has split into rival factions loyal to different teachers, prompting a blunt question about whether Christ himself has been divided.

verses.text: “Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?”

events.title: The Foolishness of the Cross: God's Wisdom, Not the World's
events.detail: A message that looks like foolishness to those perishing is, to those being saved, the power of God: Paul reminds a status-conscious church that God deliberately chose what the world considers foolish, weak, and despised.

verses.text: “The word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.”
“God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the things which are strong.”

eras.label: Era Two · 1 Corinthians 2
eras.name: Not Wisdom of Words, But the Spirit's Power
eras.dates: Paul defends his own unimpressive preaching style before turning to a wisdom only the Spirit can reveal

events.title: Paul's Preaching: In Weakness and Trembling
events.detail: Paul admits he came to Corinth without eloquence or persuasive argument, deliberately preaching only Christ crucified, so their faith would rest on God's power rather than human cleverness.

verses.text: “I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.”

events.title: God's Hidden Wisdom: We Have the Mind of Christ
events.detail: A wisdom hidden from the rulers of this age, predestined before time began, is revealed to believers through the Spirit, who alone searches even the depths of God, closing in the claim that believers possess the mind of Christ.

verses.text: “To us God revealed them through the Spirit, for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God.”
“Who has known the mind of the Lord, that he will direct Him? But we have the mind of Christ.”

eras.label: Era Three · 1 Corinthians 3
eras.name: Infants in Christ — God's Field, God's Building
eras.dates: Spiritual immaturity is diagnosed directly, then pictured through farming and construction

events.title: Still Fleshly: Milk, Not Solid Food
events.detail: Jealousy and strife prove the Corinthians are still spiritual infants: Paul reduces the personality cults to nothing more than servants planting and watering while only God causes any growth.

verses.text: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing the growth. So then neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God who causes the growth.”

events.title: Building on the Foundation: Tested by Fire
events.detail: Christ alone is the foundation any builder can lay, but what's built on top, whether gold or wood, will be tested by fire on the day of judgment, with the builder's own salvation secure either way.

verses.text: “No one can lay a foundation other than the one which is laid, which is Jesus Christ.”

events.title: You Are God's Temple: All Things Belong to You
events.detail: The church itself is called a sanctuary where God's Spirit dwells, warned against destruction, and Paul closes by reversing the factional boasting entirely: Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, all belong to them, because they belong to Christ.

verses.text: “Do you not know that you are a sanctuary of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?”

eras.label: Era Four · 1 Corinthians 4
eras.name: Stewards of the Mysteries — Fools for Christ
eras.dates: Apostolic humility set against a church that had grown arrogant enough to think it was already reigning

events.title: Stewards Judged Only by the Lord
events.detail: Paul refuses to be judged by any human court, including his own self-examination, since only the Lord's judgment on the last day will bring hidden motives to light.

verses.text: “Do not go on passing judgment before the time, but wait until the Lord comes who will both bring to light the things hidden in the darkness and make manifest the motives of hearts.”

events.title: Fools for Christ: A Spectacle to the World
events.detail: A biting, ironic contrast: the Corinthians act as though they've already arrived at kingship, while the apostles who brought them the gospel are hungry, homeless, and treated as the scum of the earth.

verses.text: “We are fools for the sake of Christ, but you are prudent in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong!”

events.title: A Father's Appeal: Sending Timothy
events.detail: Paul reframes the whole confrontation as fatherly love, not shame, sending Timothy ahead of his own visit, and warns the puffed-up that when he comes, he'll test not their words but their actual power.

verses.text: “If you were to have countless tutors in Christ, yet you would not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.”

eras.label: Era Five · 1 Corinthians 5
eras.name: Remove the Immoral Brother
eras.dates: A case of sexual immorality worse than anything among pagans, tolerated and even boasted about

events.title: Sexual Immorality Tolerated: Deliver Him to Satan
events.detail: A man is living with his father's wife, and instead of mourning, the church is proud: Paul orders formal church discipline, handing the man over for the destruction of the flesh so his spirit might ultimately be saved.

verses.text: “There is sexual immorality among you… of such a kind as does not exist even among the Gentiles… And you have become puffed up and have not mourned instead.”

events.title: A Little Leaven: Christ Our Passover Lamb
events.detail: Tolerated sin is compared to leaven that spreads through a whole batch of dough: believers are told to clear it out entirely, since Christ himself has already been sacrificed as their Passover lamb.

verses.text: “Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump… For Christ, our Passover lamb, also was sacrificed.”

events.title: Do Not Associate With a So-Called Brother in Sin
events.detail: Paul clarifies an earlier, now-lost letter: the command not to associate with immoral people was never about avoiding the world entirely, but about not tolerating unrepentant sin inside the church itself.

verses.text: “Are you not to judge those who are within the church? But those who are outside, God will judge. Remove the wicked man from among yourselves.”

eras.label: Era Six · 1 Corinthians 6
eras.name: Lawsuits and the Body as God's Temple
eras.dates: Believers suing believers in pagan courts, and a body theology that treats sexual sin as uniquely serious

events.title: Lawsuits Before Unbelievers
events.detail: Believers destined to judge the world and even angels are dragging each other into secular courts: Paul asks why they wouldn't rather be wronged than damage their witness this way.

verses.text: “It is already a failure for you, that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?”

events.title: The Unrighteous Will Not Inherit the Kingdom: But You Were Washed
events.detail: A vice list is followed immediately by grace: some of the Corinthians used to be exactly these things, but were washed, sanctified, and justified in Christ's name: identity, not just behavior, has changed.

verses.text: “Such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.”

events.title: Flee Sexual Immorality: Your Body Is a Sanctuary
events.detail: Against a slogan claiming 'all things are lawful,' Paul argues the body itself belongs to the Lord, not to be joined to sin: it's a temple of the Holy Spirit, bought at a price, meant to glorify God.

verses.text: “Your body is a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit who is in you… you were bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body.”

eras.label: Era Seven · 1 Corinthians 7
eras.name: Instructions on Marriage and Singleness
eras.dates: Answering direct questions from the Corinthians' own letter, on marriage, divorce, and staying as one was called

events.title: Marriage Duties: Better to Marry Than to Burn
events.detail: Answering a question the Corinthians had written him about, Paul addresses the marriage relationship's mutual obligations, recommending marriage as the practical answer to unchecked desire.

verses.text: “If they do not have self-control, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn with passion.”

events.title: Do Not Divorce: Even a Believer Married to an Unbeliever
events.detail: Paul distinguishes the Lord's own teaching against divorce from his own pastoral guidance for mixed marriages: an unbelieving spouse is sanctified through the believer, and the marriage should be preserved if the unbeliever is willing.

verses.text: “How do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O husband, whether you will save your wife?”

events.title: Remain in the Condition You Were Called
events.detail: Circumcised or not, slave or free: Paul's general principle is that conversion doesn't require changing one's social situation, since a believing slave is already the Lord's freedman in spirit.

verses.text: “You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.”

events.title: The Present Distress: Undistracted Devotion to the Lord
events.detail: Paul recommends singleness given 'the present distress,' arguing an unmarried person can devote themselves to the Lord's work without the divided concerns marriage inevitably brings, while clarifying marriage itself is no sin.

verses.text: “This I say for your own benefit, not to put a restraint upon you, but to promote propriety and undistracted devotion to the Lord.”

eras.label: Era Eight · 1 Corinthians 8
eras.name: Food Sacrificed to Idols — Love Builds Up
eras.dates: A question of conscience over meat sold in the marketplace, answered by prioritizing a weaker believer over one's own liberty

events.title: Knowledge Puffs Up, Love Builds Up
events.detail: Paul reframes the whole debate over idol-meat before it even starts: correct knowledge isn't the highest value; love that considers another person is.

verses.text: “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.”

events.title: An Idol Is Nothing: But Watch the Weak Conscience
events.detail: Paul agrees theologically that idols have no real existence, so meat sacrificed to them carries no spiritual contamination, but insists that exercising this freedom carelessly can wound a weaker believer's conscience and even destroy their faith.

verses.text: “If food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again—ever, so that I will not cause my brother to stumble.”

eras.label: Era Nine · 1 Corinthians 9
eras.name: Paul's Rights Surrendered — Becoming All Things to All Men
eras.dates: Paul defends his own apostolic rights only to explain, at length, why he voluntarily gave them up

events.title: An Apostle's Right to Support
events.detail: Paul defends his full apostolic rights, including financial support, arguing from ordinary human logic (soldiers, vineyard workers, oxen treading grain) and from the Lord's own command that gospel workers should live from the gospel.

verses.text: “The Lord directed those who proclaim the gospel to get their living from the gospel.”

events.title: Refusing His Own Right: An Empty Boast Avoided
events.detail: Having just proven his right to support, Paul reveals he never used it, preaching free of charge, under a compulsion he describes almost as a woe, so that his ministry can never be reduced to a paid job.

verses.text: “If I proclaim the gospel, I have nothing to boast, for I am under compulsion. For woe is me if I do not proclaim the gospel.”

events.title: Becoming All Things to All Men
events.detail: One of Paul's most quoted statements of missionary strategy: free from everyone, he made himself a slave to everyone, adapting his approach to Jew, Gentile, and the weak alike, all for the sake of winning some.

verses.text: “I have become all things to all men, so that I may by all means save some.”

events.title: Running the Race: Disciplining the Body
events.detail: Athletic imagery closes the chapter: a runner competing for an incorruptible crown, disciplining his own body so that after preaching to others he himself won't be disqualified.

verses.text: “I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that, after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.”

eras.label: Era Ten · 1 Corinthians 10
eras.name: Israel's Wilderness Warnings — Flee Idolatry
eras.dates: The wilderness generation becomes a cautionary tale, applied directly to a church still negotiating with idol worship

events.title: Israel's Example in the Wilderness: A Way of Escape
events.detail: Israel had every spiritual privilege (the cloud, the sea, spiritual food and drink from Christ himself) yet fell into idolatry and immorality in the wilderness, written down as a direct warning, closing in a promise that God always provides a way out of temptation.

verses.text: “God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will provide the way of escape also.”

events.title: Flee Idolatry: The Cup of the Lord, Not the Cup of Demons
events.detail: Sharing the Lord's Supper and sharing in pagan sacrificial meals are treated as mutually exclusive acts of loyalty: believers cannot partake at both the Lord's table and the table of demons.

verses.text: “You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.”

events.title: Whatever You Do, Do All to the Glory of God
events.detail: Practical resolution to the idol-meat question: eat what's sold in the market without interrogation, but defer to a host or fellow believer's conscience when it's directly raised: the guiding principle is seeking others' good, not just personal freedom.

verses.text: “Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 1 Corinthians 11
eras.name: Head Coverings and the Lord's Supper
eras.dates: Two worship controversies: what to wear while praying, and how the church's shared meal had become a source of shame

events.title: Head Coverings in Worship
events.detail: One of the most culturally-debated passages in Paul's letters, addressing head coverings for men and women praying or prophesying: argued from creation order, cultural custom, and appeals to what 'nature itself' teaches.

verses.text: “In the Lord, neither is woman independent of man, nor is man independent of woman… all things originate from God.”

events.title: Divisions at the Lord's Supper: One Hungry, Another Drunk
events.detail: What should be a shared meal has become a display of social inequality: wealthier members eating their own food before the poor even arrive, shaming those who have nothing.

verses.text: “In your eating each one takes his own supper first, and one is hungry and another is drunk… Do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing?”

events.title: The Institution of the Lord's Supper
events.detail: Paul relays the earliest written account of the Last Supper's institution, tracing it back to what he himself received from the Lord: bread as Christ's body, the cup as the new covenant in his blood.

verses.text: “This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me… This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”

events.title: Examine Yourselves Before Eating
events.detail: Eating and drinking without judging the body rightly, likely a reference to the very class divisions just described, has left the church weak, sick, and grieving, so Paul calls for self-examination and waiting for one another.

verses.text: “A man must test himself, and in so doing he is to eat of the bread and drink of the cup.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 1 Corinthians 12
eras.name: One Body, Many Gifts
eras.dates: Spiritual gifts distributed by one Spirit for the common good, pictured through the most detailed body metaphor in the New Testament

events.title: Varieties of Gifts, the Same Spirit
events.detail: Only the Spirit can produce a genuine confession that Jesus is Lord, and that same Spirit distributes a whole range of gifts, wisdom, healing, tongues, prophecy, to individuals exactly as he wills, not as they choose.

verses.text: “One and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each one individually just as He wills.”

events.title: The Body Has Many Members
events.detail: An extended body metaphor argues that every member, however unimpressive, is indispensable: the eye can't tell the hand it isn't needed, and the parts that seem weaker actually receive greater honor within the body.

verses.text: “The eye cannot say to the hand, ‘I have no need of you’; or again the head to the feet, ‘I have no need of you.’”
“If one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 1 Corinthians 13
eras.name: The Love Chapter
eras.dates: The most famous chapter Paul ever wrote, placed deliberately between two chapters about competing spiritual gifts

events.title: Love Is Patient, Love Is Kind
events.detail: Every impressive spiritual gift (tongues of angels, prophetic knowledge, mountain-moving faith) is declared worthless without love, which is then described not as a feeling but as a list of concrete, patient actions.

verses.text: “If I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.”
“Love is patient, love is kind, is not jealous, does not brag, is not puffed up.”

events.title: Now I Know in Part: Faith, Hope, Love
events.detail: Prophecy and knowledge are partial and temporary, destined to pass away, but love never fails: the chapter closes naming three things that remain, with love ranked as the greatest of all.

verses.text: “Now we see in a mirror dimly, but then face to face… abide faith, hope, love—these three; but the greatest of these is love.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 1 Corinthians 14
eras.name: Prophecy Greater Than Tongues — Order in Worship
eras.dates: A practical ranking of spiritual gifts by how much they build up the whole church, not just the individual using them

events.title: Prophecy Edifies the Church More Than Tongues
events.detail: Tongues without interpretation speak only to God, while prophecy edifies the whole gathered church: Paul, though he speaks in tongues more than anyone, prefers five intelligible words to ten thousand in a tongue.

verses.text: “In the church I desire to speak five words with my mind so that I may instruct others also, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.”

events.title: Tongues for Unbelievers, Prophecy for Believers
events.detail: Paul distinguishes the sign-function of tongues to outsiders from prophecy's power to convict: an unbeliever walking into unintelligible tongues will think the church insane, but prophecy can expose the secrets of a heart and drive someone to worship.

verses.text: “The secrets of his heart are disclosed; and so he will fall on his face and worship God, declaring that surely God is among you.”

events.title: Let All Things Be Done Properly and in Order
events.detail: Concrete rules for orderly worship (limited numbers speaking in tongues with interpretation, prophets speaking one at a time) include a much-debated instruction for women to keep silent in the churches, one of the most contested passages in the letter.

verses.text: “God is not a God of confusion but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.”
“All things must be done properly and in an orderly manner.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 1 Corinthians 15
eras.name: The Resurrection of the Dead
eras.dates: The letter's longest single argument, defending the bodily resurrection against Corinthians who apparently denied it outright

events.title: The Gospel Received: Witnessed by More Than Five Hundred
events.detail: Paul recites what is likely the earliest written creed in the New Testament: Christ died, was buried, was raised, and appeared to Cephas, the Twelve, over five hundred believers at once, James, and finally to Paul himself.

verses.text: “Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and that He was buried, and that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.”
“He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom remain until now, but some have fallen asleep.”

events.title: If Christ Has Not Been Raised, Your Faith Is Worthless
events.detail: Against those denying any resurrection of the dead, Paul follows the logic to its devastating conclusion: if Christ himself wasn't raised, the whole faith collapses and believers are, of all people, most to be pitied.

verses.text: “If Christ has not been raised, your faith is worthless; you are still in your sins.”

events.title: Christ the Firstfruits: So That God May Be All in All
events.detail: Christ's resurrection is described as the firstfruits of a larger harvest, as death entered through one man, resurrection comes through another, ending in a vision of the Son handing the kingdom back to the Father so God is all in all.

verses.text: “As in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.”

events.title: Sown Perishable, Raised Imperishable
events.detail: Paul answers skeptical questions about what a resurrection body could even look like, using a seed's transformation as an analogy: sown in weakness and dishonor, raised in power and glory as a genuinely new kind of body.

verses.text: “It is sown a corruptible body, it is raised an incorruptible body; it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory… it is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body.”

events.title: Death Is Swallowed Up in Victory
events.detail: The chapter climaxes in a triumphant mystery (not everyone will die, but everyone will be changed in an instant at the last trumpet) closing with a taunt aimed directly at death itself, now stripped of its sting.

verses.text: “Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 1 Corinthians 16
eras.name: The Collection and Final Greetings
eras.dates: Practical closing business: a relief fund for Jerusalem, travel plans, and one word of Aramaic left untranslated

events.title: The Collection for the Saints in Jerusalem
events.detail: Paul organizes a weekly, proportional savings plan so the collection for Jerusalem's poor believers will be ready when he arrives, rather than requiring a last-minute scramble.

verses.text: “On the first day of every week each one of you is to set something aside, saving whatever he has prospered, so that no collections be made when I come.”

events.title: Travel Plans: A Wide and Effective Door at Ephesus
events.detail: Paul explains his own itinerary through Macedonia, his hope to spend real time in Corinth, and commends both Timothy and Apollos for their coming visits, while staying himself in Ephesus a while longer.

verses.text: “A wide and effective door has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.”

events.title: Be Watchful, Stand Firm, Act Like Men, Be Strong
events.detail: A rapid four-part charge closes the practical body of the letter, followed immediately by a reminder that every instruction given should ultimately be carried out in love.

verses.text: “Let all that you do be done in love.”

events.title: Closing Greetings: ‘Maranatha’
events.detail: Names, greetings, and Paul's own handwritten sign-off close the letter, ending in an untranslated Aramaic prayer ('Maranatha,' meaning 'Our Lord, come') one of the earliest surviving prayers of the church.

verses.text: “If anyone does not love the Lord, he is to be accursed. Maranatha.” — an Aramaic phrase, likely meaning 'Our Lord, come,' left untranslated as an early liturgical prayer.
